questions.question:
An ideal gas expands in such a way that the product of its pressure and the cube of its absolute temperature remains constant during the process. That is, the relation: \(PT^3=\text{constant}.\) Under these conditions, what is the coefficient of volume expansion of the gas?

1.\(\dfrac{1}{T}\)2.\(\dfrac{2}{T}\)
3.\(\dfrac{4}{T}\)4.\(\dfrac{3}{T}\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(\gamma= \left ( \dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \right )\dfrac{1}{\Delta T} \) Step:Find the coefficient of volume expansion of the gas. \(PT^3=\text {constant}\) \(\Rightarrow \dfrac{RT}{V}\times T^3=\text {constant}~~~[\because PV=nRT]\) \(\Rightarrow T^4V^{-1}=\text {constant}\) By taking log on both sides, we get; \(\Rightarrow 4log(T)-log(V)=\text{constant}\) \(\Rightarrow \dfrac{4\Delta T}{T}-\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}=0\) \(\Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta V}{V}=\dfrac{4\Delta T}{T}\) The coefficient of volume expansion is given by: \(\gamma= \left ( \dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \right )\dfrac{1}{\Delta T} \) Therefore; \(\Rightarrow \gamma= \dfrac{4}{T}\) Hence, option (3) is the correct answer.

Hint:\(\Delta V =V_0\gamma \Delta T\) Step: Find the cube's volume increase due to this heating. questions.question:
When the temperature of a metal wire is increased from \(0^\circ ~\mathrm{C}\) to \(10^\circ ~\mathrm{C},\) its length increases by \(0.02\%.\) What is the percentage decrease in its mass density?
1. \(0.008\)%
2. \(0.06\)%
3. \(0.8\)%
4. \(2.3\)%
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}=-\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}\) Step: Find the percentage decrease in its mass density. Mass density is given by: \(\rho=\dfrac{M}{V}\) \(\Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}=-\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}~~~[\because M=\text{constant}]\) \(\Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}=-\dfrac{\Delta l}{l}-\dfrac{\Delta A}{A}~~~[\because V=l\times A]\) \(\Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}=-\dfrac{\Delta l}{l}-2\alpha\Delta T\) \(\Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}=-\dfrac{\Delta l}{l}-\dfrac{2\Delta l}{l}~~~\left[\because \dfrac{\Delta l}{l}=\alpha\Delta T\right] \) \(\Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}=-\dfrac{3\Delta l}{l}\) \(\Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}=-3\times0.02\% ~~~\left[\text{Given};\dfrac{\Delta l}{l} =0.02\%\right]\) \(\Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}=-0.06\% \) Therefore, the percentage decrease in its mass density is\(0.06\%.\) Hence, option (2) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
A uniform cylindrical rod of length \(L\) and radius \(r,\) is made from a material whose Young’s modulus of Elasticity equals \(Y.\) When this rod is heated by temperature \(T\) and simultaneously subjected to a net longitudinal compressional force \(F,\) its length remains unchanged. The coefficient of volume expansion, of the material of the rod, is (nearly) equal to:

1.\(\dfrac{3F}{\pi r^2YT}\)2.\(\dfrac{6F}{\pi r^2YT}\)
3.\(\dfrac{F}{\pi r^2YT}\)4.\(\dfrac{9F}{\pi r^2YT}\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(\Delta l=l \alpha \Delta T\) Step 1:Find the value of compressive and thermal strain. As the length of the rod remains unchanged, The strain caused by compressive forces is equal and opposite to the thermal strain. Now, compressive strain is obtained by using the formula for Young's modulus we get; \(\Rightarrow Y=\frac{F\times l}{A\times \Delta l}\) The compressive strain is given by; \(\frac{\Delta l}{l}=\frac{F}{A Y}=\frac{F}{\pi Y r^2} ~~~...(1)\) Also, thermal strain in the rod is obtained by using the formula for expansion in the rod is given by; \(Δl=lαΔT\) \(⇒ \text{Thermal strain}, \frac{Δl​}{l}=αΔT~~~...(2)\) Step 2:Find the coefficient of volume expansion, of the material. From the equations \((1)\) and \((2)\), we get; \( \frac{F}{\pi r^2 Y}=\alpha T \quad[\because \Delta T=T] \) \( \Rightarrow \alpha=\frac{F}{\pi r^2 Y T} \) Therefore, the coefficient of volumetric expansion of the rod is given by; \(\Rightarrow\gamma=3 \alpha=\frac{3 F}{\pi r^2 Y T} \) Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
The pressure that has to be applied to the ends of a steel wire of length \(10~\text{cm}\) to keep its length constant when its temperature is raised by \(100^\circ \text{C}\) is:
(Young's modulus of steel is \(2\times 10^{11}~\text{Nm}^{-2}\) and coefficient of thermal expansion is \(1.1 \times 10^{-5}~\text{K}^{-1}\))
1. \( 2.2 \times 10^9 ~\text{Pa} \)
2. \( 2.2 \times 10^7 ~\text{Pa} \)
3. \( 2.2 \times 10^6 ~\text{Pa} \)
4. \( 2.2 \times 10^8 ~\text{Pa} \)
questions.explanation:
Hint:The thermal stress developed in wire\(=Y \alpha \Delta T\) Step: Find the thermal stress developed in the wire. Given: \(l = 10~\text{cm}, \Delta T = 100^{\circ}\text{C}, Y = 2\times 10^{11}~\text{N/m}^2, \alpha = 1.1\times 10^{-5}~\text{K}^{-1}\) The thermal stress developed in the steel wire is given by; \(\sigma_\text{thermal}= Y \alpha \Delta T\) \(\Rightarrow \sigma_\text{thermal}= 2\times 10^{11}\times 1.1\times 10^{-5}\times 100\) \(\Rightarrow \sigma_\text{thermal}= 2.2\times 10^{8}~\text{N/m}^2\) Since the pressure developed in the wire is equal to the thermal stress developed. Therefore, the pressure applied to the ends of the wire is\(2.2\times 10^{8}~\text{Pa}\). Hence, option (4) is the correct answer.

An external pressure \(P\) is applied on a cube at \(0^\circ\text{C}\) so that it is equally compressed from all sides. \(K\) is the bulk modulus of the material of the cube and \(\alpha\) is its coefficient of linear expansion. Suppose we want to bring the cube to its original size by heating. The temperature should be raised by:
1. \( \dfrac{{P}}{3 \alpha {K}}\)

2. \( \dfrac{{P}}{\alpha{K}} \)

3. \( \dfrac{3 \alpha}{{PK}} \)

4. \(3 {PK} \alpha\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\({B}=\frac{-{P}}{\frac{{dV}}{{V}}}\) Step 1: Use the bulk modulus relation. \(K = \dfrac{P}{\Delta V/V} \ \ \ \Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta V}{V} = \dfrac{P}{K}\) Step 2: Use volume expansion due to heating. For an isotropic solid, \(\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} = 3\alpha\Delta T\) To restore the cube to its original size, \(3\alpha\Delta T = \dfrac{P}{K} \\ \therefore \Delta T = \dfrac{P}{3\alpha K}\) Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.
